raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Qwen-Image 2.1 requests with dimensions not divisible by 32 can fail validation. Saving its RGBA outputs as JPEG also raises an encoding error.

## Modifications

- Align positive request dimensions to multiples of 32, with a minimum of 32 pixels. For example, 1280x720 becomes 1280x704.
- Apply the same alignment to synthetic warmup requests.
- Composite RGBA images onto a white background before JPG/JPEG encoding, preserving PNG transparency and the original image array.
- Add regression coverage for request parsing, CLI parameters, warmup, and output saving.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated with Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo using the native SGLang backend and Torch SDPA.

- 118 unit tests passed with no skips: 90 in `test_qwen_image21.py` and 28 in `test_output_saving.py`.
- HTTP generation verified aligned dimensions, JPEG/RGB output, PNG/RGBA output, explicit dimension overrides, and rejection of invalid dimensions.
- Synthetic warmup passed in both eager and breakable CUDA graph modes.
- BCG capture was verified, and two consecutive JPEG requests succeeded without a graph-miss warning.
- CLI `--720p` successfully saved a 1280x704 JPEG.

The complete validation script exited with code 0.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This change does not modify model forward code, denoising, or kernels. No inference speedup is claimed.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

The fix looks reasonable. Could you simplify the new tests, especially `TestQwenImage21Resolution`, before merging?

- Use the file's existing pytest style with parameterized cases for the alignment rules. Direct `QwenImage21SamplingParams` construction is sufficient for most dimension cases; keep the server-args fixture limited to the integration checks.
- In `test_request_alignment_precedes_pipeline_validation`, keep a focused request-to-validation regression, but remove `batch.log()` (there is no log assertion), the checks of unchanged latent-shape arithmetic, and the repeated `replace(sampling)` check for every dimension. The legacy-Qwen check can also assert directly on its sampling parameters.
- Keep the HTTP/CLI parameter-merging and synthetic-warmup regressions, plus coverage that zero/negative dimensions are still rejected. The `_explicit_fields` assertion can be dropped unless there is a specific metadata regression it is intended to protect.
- The output-saving tests are already fairly focused. Please retain the alpha-compositing, PNG transparency, and input-array non-mutation checks.

Also, please update the title to the required format, for example: `[Fix] diffusion: Align Qwen-Image 2.1 resolution and handle RGBA JPEG output`.

Thanks for the review! I simplified the resolution tests to use the existing pytest style with parameterized cases and direct sampling-parameter construction. The server-args fixture is now limited to integration checks.

I removed the redundant logging, latent-shape, replace(), and _explicit_fields checks, while retaining the request-to-validation, HTTP/CLI merging, synthetic-warmup, and invalid-dimension regressions. The output-saving tests remain intact.

Both test files pass: 129 tests passed.

@@ -14,6 +17,34 @@ class QwenImage21SamplingParams(SamplingParams):
     num_inference_steps: int = 40

+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        super().__post_init__()
+        self._align_resolution()
+
+    def prepare_synthetic_warmup_request_for_queue(self, req, server_args) -> None:
+        # Warmup copies sampling defaults, then overwrites their dimensions
+        # without invoking the dataclass constructor again.
+        self._align_resolution()
+
+    def _align_resolution(self) -> None:
+        requested_size = (self.width, self.height)
+        # Match Diffusers before request batching and pipeline validation
+        # consume these dimensions.
+        # Keep a positive sub-grid request usable, but leave invalid dimensions
+        # to the existing request validation instead of rounding them positive.
+        if self.width is not None and self.width > 0:
+            self.width = max(32, self.width // 32 * 32)
+        if self.height is not None and self.height > 0:
+            self.height = max(32, self.height // 32 * 32)
+        if (self.width, self.height) != requested_size:
+            logger.warning(
+                "Qwen-Image 2.1 requires dimensions divisible by 32; adjusted "
+                "requested resolution from %sx%s to %sx%s",
+                *requested_size,
+                self.width,
+                self.height,
+            )
+
     @classmethod
     def default_image_output_format(cls) -> str:
         """Preserve Qwen-Image 2.1's RGBA outputs by default."""

+    expected = (np.array([20, 80, 160]) * alpha + 255 * (255 - alpha) + 127) // 255
